title: The Export sheet lets you pick the size of the video
goal: A Retina screen recording is 2880 by 1800 or larger, and the Export sheet can only write it at that size: a five minute edit was estimated at 678 MB. Premiere and every share tool offer 1080p and 720p, which is what people post. Add a size choice to video export.
notes: Found by measure-the-video-editor-against-premiere-and-fi (2026-09-24); gap report docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md. Reproduced: five-minute walk exportDialogAsVideo on a 2880x1800 recording: rows are Format, Quality, Captions only; footer '2880 x 1800 px, 30 fps, 5:00, about 678 MB' (export-sheet-5-min.jpg). Rows live in Sources/Photonz/VideoExportDialog.swift. The size estimate itself being off is the-export-sheet-s-size-for-an-edited-video-is-c; do not fix that here.
acceptance: The Export sheet for MP4 (and GIF) has a Size row: Full, 1080p, 720p, and the full size is named in pixels
Picking a smaller size changes the size estimate and the written file's pixel size
The choice is remembered for the next export
A walk exports the five minute recording at 1080p and the file is 1728x1080 (aspect kept)
For an edited video made of screen recordings, the size the sheet shows is within a factor of two of the file written at the same setting, and still says about
an-editing-session-walk's export step logs a sheet size and a written size that agree within that factor
Works at Next defaults with no switch turned on, and an audit written under queue/audits/ gives the try steps and a real picture
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: digest 2026-09-24: folded in the-export-sheet-s-size-for-an-edited-video-is-c. The sheet told a person an edited 21 second video would be about 9.6 MB and the MP4 came out at 0.7 MB (an-editing-session-walk export step, queue/audits/2026-09-24-editing-session-walk.json). The 678 MB estimate for five minutes in this task's goal may be inflated by the same fault, so fix the estimate while adding the size row: one sheet, one number people can trust.

Adversarial review before building: a Premiere user expects Resolution (Match Source, 1080p, 720p) apart from bitrate, so Size is its own row and owns the pixels while Quality keeps frame rate and budget. The old Quality presets secretly shrank an MP4 (Standard 1440, Small 960 long side) with nothing saying so; with a Size row that coupling goes (only on the Next sheet; the Current recording sheet passes no size and is byte-identical). 1080p means short side 1080, so 2880x1800 -> 1728x1080 and portrait works. Sizes that would not shrink the recording are hidden; with only Full left the row goes. GIF/HEIC get Full, 720p, 480p (default 480p) instead of Full, 1080p, 720p: a 1080p GIF is a file nobody can send and 480p is where the old Standard GIF was (800x500). MP4 defaults to Full so an untouched recording still leaves as a verbatim copy. Mock check: export-share.html part A draws Format / Scale / Quality as segmented rows with a pixel summary; the Size row follows that shape.

Reproduced the estimate fault before fixing it: an-edited-recording-comes-out-as-a-video-walk, 4 s cut of the sample: sheet 'about 1.8 MB', 73 KB landed (25x); 14 s mix: 'about 6.4 MB', 171 KB landed. Cause: an edited document has no one file to measure, so the sheet fell back to the encoder budget, a ceiling a screen recording never nears. Fix: measure the footage the clips play (bytes per pixel-second across the recording files) and add an allowance for burned-in captions (measured: 1080p re-encode of the Retina talk is 227 kbps without captions, 404 kbps with the lit word moving). After: 74 KB vs 73 KB, 74 KB vs 74 KB, 258 KB vs 171 KB (1.5x).
